subject: CFA with covariates (MIMIC) and reliability problems

messages.author: d22416daf1c84669
messages.subject: CFA with covariates (MIMIC) and reliability problems
parts:
Dear cfa expert,
I have used and got fine results with a cfa model with TA as covariate:
Faktorer.TA<- '
    f1 =~ x3+x6+x9
    f2=~ x1+x2+x4+x5+x7+x8    
    f3 =~ x10+x11+x12+x13+x14+x15+x16+x17  
   f1 + f2 + f3 ~ TA
 '
fit.TA <- cfa(Faktorer.TA, data = Activ.x,meanstructure=FALSE, estimator="DWLS",std.lv=TRUE)

When using the reliability function, I got the error message below:   

> reliability(fit.TA)

Error in ly[[i]] %*% ve[[i]] : non-conformable arguments

In addition: Warning message:

In (apply(ly[[i]], 2, sum)^2) * diag(ve[[i]]) :

  longer object length is not a multiple of shorter object length

A similar cfa model without the covariate TA gave no error message

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: CFA with covariates (MIMIC) and reliability problems
parts: fit.TA <- cfa(Faktorer.TA, data = Activ.x,meanstructure=FALSE, estimator="DWLS",std.lv=TRUE)

Don't set meanstructure=FALSE, I don't even think that is allowed when estimator="DWLS" because it needs a mean structure.

I think with DWLS, there might be a problem because by default, conditional.x=TRUE.  Perhaps setting that to FALSE would prevent the error.  In any case, reliability() is deprecated in the latest semTools, in favor of the more well-designed compRelSEM().

https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/semTools/news/news.html
